What impossible hypothesis should we tes.text: Home · Your analyses · Guest demo session Leave demo Meta Platforms, Inc. What impossible hypothesis should we test? Meta Platforms, Inc.'s separately reported businesses may be worth more as one platform others build on than as 2 products it sells.: It reports 2 segments — Family of Apps (FoA), Reality Labs (RL) — which means it already operates the shared substrate underneath them. A substrate that carries several first-party businesses can usually carry third-party ones at close to zero marginal cost, and the economics of the two are not the same.; The workflow that Meta Platforms, Inc.'s product sits inside may stop existing rather than be improved.: It sells competitive compensation and a wide range of benefits, including many learning and development resources. A product priced against a human process captures a share of that process's cost; when the process is performed by a machine end to end, the customer is no longer buying a better way to do it, and there is nothing left for the price to be a share of.; The advertiser spending the budget on its own channels may be structurally unable to answer a move here, which would make the contested position far cheaper to take than a symmetric reading implies.: The advertiser spending the budget on its own channels was established as a competitor from disclosure rather than assumed.
